function pairs(args, allowed, switches = []) {
  const values = new Map();
  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index++) {
    const key = args[index];
    if (!allowed.includes(key) && !switches.includes(key) || values.has(key)) throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Unknown or repeated option: ' + key);
    if (switches.includes(key)) { values.set(key, true); continue; }
    const value = args[++index];
    if (!value || value.startsWith('--')) throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Missing value for ' + key);
    values.set(key, value);
  }
  return values;
}
function portNumber(value, fallback) {
  if (value === undefined) return fallback;
  if (!/^\d{1,5}$/.test(String(value)) || Number(value) > 65535) throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Port must be 0–65535.');
  return Number(value);
}
export async function startMerchantMcp({ configPath, port = 3211, tokenEnv = 'MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN',
  environment = process.env, stellarExpertFetchImpl, woocommerceFetchImpl, mppFetchImpl, oauthConfigPath, oauthFetchImpl, accounting, consoleDirectory, consoleBinding, providerOptions = {} } = {}) {
  if (!configPath || !/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/.test(tokenEnv)) throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Supply a merchant configuration and token environment-variable name.');
  const providerPrototype = providerOptions && typeof providerOptions === 'object' ? Object.getPrototypeOf(providerOptions) : undefined;
  if (providerPrototype !== Object.prototype && providerPrototype !== null)
    throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'Supply a plain providerOptions object for trusted native startup.');
  port = portNumber(port, 3211);
  const operator = await openMerchantOperator(configPath,
    { environment, stellarExpert: { environment, fetchImpl: stellarExpertFetchImpl }, woocommerce: { environment, fetchImpl: woocommerceFetchImpl }, mpp: { environment, fetchImpl: mppFetchImpl }, opensearch: { environment }, opencage: { env: environment }, grpc: { environment }, openapi: { environment }, arcgis: { environment }, opendatasoft: { environment }, accounting: { ...accounting, environment }, ...providerOptions });
  let server, access, operatorConsole, draining=false;
  try {
    access = await loadOAuthResourceHost({configPath:oauthConfigPath ?? environment.MCP_OAUTH_CONFIG,
      bearerToken:environment[tokenEnv],fetchImpl:oauthFetchImpl});
    const handler = createMcpToolHandler(operator, { ...access.transportOptions, maxRequestBytes: operator.maxRequestBytes,
      allowedClientOrigins: String(environment.MCP_CLIENT_ORIGINS ?? '').split(',').map(value => value.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      serverName: 'starforge-merchant-operator', serverVersion: '0.1.0',
      instructions: merchantInstructions(operator.tools) });
    if (consoleBinding !== undefined && consoleDirectory === undefined)
      throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR', 'A managed console binding requires its original console directory.');
    if(consoleDirectory!==undefined){
      if(typeof consoleDirectory!=='string'||!consoleDirectory)throw failure('CONFIGURATION_ERROR','Supply a private operator console directory.');
      operatorConsole=await (await import('./console/service.mjs')).createMerchantConsole({
        operator,configPath,directory:consoleDirectory,...access.transportOptions,binding:consoleBinding});
    }
    const routed=operatorConsole?async(req,res)=>{
      try{
        if(draining){
          res.writeHead(503,{'content-type':'application/json','cache-control':'no-store'});
          res.end(JSON.stringify({error:{code:'OPERATOR_CLOSING',message:'The original merchant host is closing.'}}));return;
        }
        if(await operatorConsole.handler(req,res))return;
        await handler(req,res);
      }catch(error){
        if(res.headersSent){res.destroy(error);return;}
        res.writeHead(500,{'content-type':'application/json','cache-control':'no-store'});
        res.end(JSON.stringify({error:{code:error.code??'CONSOLE_ERROR',message:'The original operator could not return this response.'}}));
      }
    }:handler;
    server = createServer(access.wrap(routed));
    server.requestTimeout = 150000; server.headersTimeout = 10000; server.keepAliveTimeout = 2000;
    await new Promise((done, reject) => {
      server.once('error', reject);
      server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', () => { server.removeListener('error', reject); done(); });
    });
  } catch (error) {
    server?.close();
    try { await operatorConsole?.close(); } finally { try { await operator.close(); } finally { await access?.close(); } }
    throw error;
  }
  let closing, stopped;
  const close = () => {
    if (closing) return closing;
    draining=true;
    closing = (async () => {
      stopped??=new Promise((done, reject) => server.close(error => error&&error.code!=='ERR_SERVER_NOT_RUNNING' ? reject(error) : done()));
      // Preserve the original customer checkpoints, then let the native owners
      // cancel/drain accepted provider work before waiting for their returns.
      try {
        operatorConsole?.beginClose();
        const results=await Promise.allSettled([operatorConsole?.close(),operator.close()]);
        const errors=results.filter(value=>value.status==='rejected').map(value=>value.reason);
        if(errors.length)throw errors.length===1?errors[0]:Object.assign(new AggregateError(errors,'Original merchant shutdown is incomplete.'),{code:'OPERATOR_SHUTDOWN_INCOMPLETE'});
      } finally {
        try { await access.close(); }
        finally { server.closeAllConnections(); await stopped; }
      }
    })();
    closing.catch(()=>{closing=undefined;});
    return closing;
  };
  const url=new URL('http://127.0.0.1:' + server.address().port).origin;
  return { operator, server, url, maxRequestBytes: operator.maxRequestBytes, authorization:access.describe(),
    ...(operatorConsole?{consoleUrl:url+'/operator/',operatorConsole}:{}),close };
}

  if (!args.length || args.length === 1 && ['--help', 'help'].includes(args[0])) { process.stdout.write(HELP); return; }

// MIT. Original tool metadata; provider runtimes load only when selected.
import { CLIENT_EXPORT_MANIFEST, CLIENT_EXPORT_FILES } from '../../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/developer/client-export-contracts.mjs';
import { MAX_RETAINED_CHUNK_BYTES } from '../retained-file-contracts.mjs';

const digest = { type: 'string', pattern: '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' };

const alias = { type: 'string', pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$' };

const tenant = { type: 'string', pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$' };

const release = { type: 'string', pattern: '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$' };

const identity = { type: 'string', minLength: 1, maxLength: 128 };

const revision = { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 };

function fleetClientTools(tool) {
  const scope = { tenant, slot: alias }, selected = { ...scope, exportId: release };
  return [
    tool('merchant_fleet_client_list', 'List original retained customer SDK exports for one declared merchant and slot. Completion receipts and interrupted exports remain available when that slot is stopped.',
      { ...scope, after: release, limit: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 50 } }, ['tenant', 'slot'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_fleet_client_status', 'Inspect the original five customer files, exact saved payment terms, completion receipt and release provenance for this merchant and slot.',
      selected, ['tenant', 'slot', 'exportId'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_fleet_client_generate', 'Generate the original customer SDK from this exact fleet-owned merchant instance into a new retained export ID. Read the actual slot instanceId from merchant_fleet_status; the source is its live original OpenAPI.',
      { ...scope, id: release, instanceId: identity }, ['tenant', 'slot', 'id', 'instanceId']),
    tool('merchant_fleet_client_adopt', 'Retain a completion receipt for the inspected original five legacy customer files in this slot. Requires their exact complete files digest and preserves all payload bytes.',
      { ...selected, expectedFilesSha256: digest }, ['tenant', 'slot', 'exportId', 'expectedFilesSha256'], { idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_fleet_client_manifest', 'Read the original customer completion manifest and its exact identity in this merchant and slot. Use its SHA-256 to select retained file downloads.',
      selected, ['tenant', 'slot', 'exportId'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_fleet_client_file', 'Read bounded SHA-pinned original customer bytes within one declared merchant, slot and export. Continue using readId, offset and inspected hashes; released or expired reads can reopen the same immutable bytes.',
      { ...selected, file: { type: 'string', enum: [CLIENT_EXPORT_MANIFEST, ...CLIENT_EXPORT_FILES] },
        expectedManifestSha256: digest, expectedSha256: digest, readId: identity,
        offset: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0 }, limit: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: MAX_RETAINED_CHUNK_BYTES } },
      ['tenant', 'slot', 'exportId', 'file', 'expectedManifestSha256'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_fleet_client_file_release', 'Release only this merchant and slot’s temporary original customer file read. The retained customer files and completion receipt remain available.',
      { ...selected, readId: identity }, ['tenant', 'slot', 'exportId', 'readId'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
  ];
}

function fleetDiscoveryTools(tool) {
  const scope = { tenant, slot: alias, instanceId: identity };
  const page = {
    view: { type: 'string', enum: ['list', 'search'] },
    limit: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 100 },
    offset: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0, maximum: 9999999 },
    query: { type: 'string', minLength: 1, maxLength: 1024 },
    cursor: { type: 'string', minLength: 1, maxLength: 512 },
    network: { type: 'string', enum: ['stellar:testnet', 'stellar:pubnet'] },
    type: { type: 'string', enum: ['http', 'mcp'] },
    scheme: { type: 'string', maxLength: 256 }, payTo: { type: 'string', maxLength: 256 },
    extensions: { type: 'string', maxLength: 256 },
  };
  return [
    tool('merchant_fleet_discovery_status', 'Read one tenant’s original seller enrollment, serving release and instance, exact payment terms, catalogue head and original buyer explorer. The signing identity belongs to the tenant across release slots. Interrupted setup includes its inspected recovery identity.',
      { tenant }, ['tenant'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_fleet_discovery_enrollment', 'Read the original public seller enrollment and pinned public key for this tenant, with its original source and accepted origin, recipients, networks and schemes.',
      { tenant }, ['tenant'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_fleet_discovery_enrollment_review', 'Review the exact serving tenant release, actual offers and source-derived permissions before original seller enrollment. For an incomplete setup, pass expectedIncompleteId from current status to review preservation of its partial files followed by enrollment.',
      { ...scope, sellerId: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,128}$' },
        sourceURL: { type: 'string', minLength: 1, maxLength: 4096 }, expectedIncompleteId: digest },
      ['tenant', 'slot', 'instanceId', 'sellerId'], { readOnly: true }),
    tool('merchant_fleet_discovery_enroll', 'Create this tenant’s original seller identity from the exact enrollment review. The current routing guard spans original setup. A reviewed incomplete setup is preserved intact before creating its replacement; completed enrollment reopens its existing identity.',

# Recurring customer work

The merchant operator keeps a complete procedure for a returning customer: who receives it, what useful output they need, which original workflow performs it, and the source and period selected for each run.

Open **Workflows → Recurring customer work** in the existing merchant Console. The same work is available through `starforge merchant-workflow-series` and the typed `MerchantWorkflowSeriesClient`.

## Complete a customer period in the browser

1. Open the original merchant profile. Save the complete native procedure in **Workflows**, or install its original [workflow recipe](WORKFLOW_RECIPES.md). Include the existing native review, publication and customer-export steps that this customer actually needs.
2. In **Recurring customer work**, choose **New series**. Select that saved workflow and name the customer, task and useful output. The series retains the exact workflow revision and its complete default inputs.
3. Choose a manual, daily, weekly or monthly calendar. Save the series edition. A calendar suggests whole periods; each cycle starts when the operator chooses **Start original workflow**.
4. Select **New period or source edition**, or choose a proposed calendar period. Enter a stable key, full period, due date, actual source reference and reason this work is useful. Review the complete inputs, including customer-specific identifiers and versions.
5. Choose **Review complete cycle**. The review shows every original native request, explicit mappings, required results and operator pauses, together with the currently configured tool contracts. Resolve a changed contract in the original workflow and select its new saved edition.
6. Choose **Save reviewed cycle**, then **Review first start**. The saved cycle can be received on another host before this review. Start it against the currently bound original host when ready.
7. Choose **Open original run and customer receiving**. All original native results, recovery, pause and handover controls remain there. On a completed customer export, use **Prepare customer** and receive its complete files in **Customers**.
8. For the next period, select the next dates and actual source. The earlier period, its complete inputs and native results remain available in the series history.

The screen retains a full pending action before dispatch. After a lost response, **Continue original action** sends the same saved request. A changed customer period uses a separately reviewed key.

## Series editions and cycle keys

A series edition contains the customer, task, selected workflow revision, complete default input object, explicit cycle mappings, calendar and whether new work is enabled. Save another edition when the procedure or customer defaults change. Existing cycles keep their selected edition.

A cycle key identifies one original customer task within the series. Its cycle ID and native run ID are derived from that series and key. The same key, source and inputs reopen the original saved work. A request that reuses the key with a different source, period or input is rejected with the original conflict.

For a corrected or changed source, choose a new readable key such as `2026-10-source-2` and link its **Earlier cycle**. Retain the actual source reference in **Selected source edition or reference** and explain the useful change. Two cycles can cover the same dates when their customer tasks differ.

Turning off **Enable new work in this series** prevents preparation and first starts. Existing original runs remain accessible through their native controls. A planned cycle can be canceled with a retained reason until its original run is reserved. After reservation, use the original run's pause, recovery and handover controls.

## Carry complete period values into native inputs

A series can map its saved cycle values into the complete workflow inputs. The original workflow then maps those inputs into its saved native requests.

For example, a workflow whose declared inputs already contain `period` and `sourceEdition` can use:

```json
{
  "baseInputs": {
    "period": { "start": "", "end": "" },
    "sourceEdition": ""
  },
  "cycleBindings": [
    { "target": "/period/start", "pointer": "/period/start" },
    { "target": "/period/end", "pointer": "/period/end" },
    { "target": "/sourceEdition", "pointer": "/sourceEdition" }
  ]
}
```

Use the actual input names and structures selected by the original workflow. Bindings target existing containers; each target receives one complete value. Supported cycle values are `/id`, `/runId`, `/key`, `/label`, `/period/start`, `/period/end`, `/dueDate`, `/sourceEdition` and `/reason`.

The complete input object is limited to 16 MiB, and the complete review/action request to 32 MiB. A period's saved source note is a reference to the actual selected material; any native source bodies or manifests needed for execution belong in the original complete workflow inputs or native source records.

Calendar dates use `YYYY-MM-DD` and inclusive period endpoints. Daily and weekly intervals advance from the saved anchor date. Monthly intervals retain the anchor's day, clipping each boundary to that month's final day. A January 31 anchor therefore produces boundaries on February 28 and March 31 in a non-leap year. Calendar queries return full periods that overlap the requested window and include `nextFrom` for the next page.

## Typed integration

The installed distribution exports `./merchant/console/series` and `./merchant/console/series-handover`, including adjacent TypeScript declarations. From a source checkout:

```js
import {
  MerchantWorkflowSeriesClient,
  writeWorkflowSeriesFile
} from './stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/console/workflow-series-client.mjs';

const client = new MerchantWorkflowSeriesClient({
  url: consoleUrl,
  tokenEnv: 'MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN',
  environment
});

try {
  const prepared = await client.prepareCycle(completePeriodRequest);
  await writeWorkflowSeriesFile('/private/operator/period-review.json', prepared);
  // Present prepared.review and later pass this same saved value to saveCycle.
  const saved = await client.saveCycle(prepared);
  const start = await client.prepareStart(saved.cycle.id);
  await writeWorkflowSeriesFile('/private/operator/period-start-review.json', start);
  // Present start.review; startCycle reopens an already-started original run.
  await client.startCycle(start);
  const progress = await client.waitCycle(saved.cycle.id, { timeoutMs: 120000 });
  console.log(progress.status);
} finally {
  client.close();
}
```

Use `list`, paged `series`, `calendar`, `cycle`, `capture` and `receive` to operate the same records. The client uses the existing Console transport, token handling, native execution owner and atomic receiving writer.

## Inspect the configured host

Opening the Host page calls the synchronous `operator.inspectHost()` snapshot. It returns the configured tools and providers without importing or constructing provider implementations. The snapshot includes:

- The merchant name, configured tool families and exact native request-byte capacity.
- Provider states and measured load duration for implementations already opened by this owner.
- The original release-source aliases.
- Active accepted calls, host shutdown state and the currently owned seller instance.
- A SHA-256 identity of the normalized configuration. The browser also receives the original configuration file's basename, byte count and SHA-256.
- A complete configured tool-definition catalog with original annotation values and exact definition digests.
- The source-owned provider declarations, their dependency graph, request limits, native concurrency/shutdown declarations and source-file digests.

The **Inspect native status** button saves and runs the original `merchant_status` tool. That explicit operation retains the full native status return and can load the configured status providers. Refreshing the lightweight host snapshot uses no native status call.

The configuration fingerprint is stable across a listener-port change. Moving or changing the configured source, workspace or release-store identity changes the fingerprint. A saved profile can be explicitly bound to the newly displayed host revision; every retained binding stays in its original profile history.

## Review host changes and retain bindings

Select a saved profile and choose **Review host**. The comparison identifies added, removed and changed native tools; configured provider declarations and borrowed dependencies; original source aliases; and native request capacity. Expand a change to inspect the complete before/after value. Search and category filters operate on this retained comparison, with fifty rows per page. A changed tool can be opened in the original Tools editor without running it.

The configured composition is captured from the actual source-owned provider registry and the exact tool definitions advertised by this operator. Each tool retains its definition SHA-256, family and original MCP annotations. Each provider retains its declaration path and SHA-256, host configuration input, dependencies, byte limit, ordinary concurrency, shutdown behavior and explicit concurrent controls. The composition contains only the configured provider roots and their transitive dependencies. Reading or comparing it opens no provider implementation.

Two stable digests cover the configured tool catalog and provider declarations. Their combined fingerprint changes with those declared capabilities. A distribution source commit, when available, is retained separately; an unrelated repository commit alone does not change the configured fingerprint. A provider-source digest identifies that declaration module. The installed distribution remains the authority for the full implementation source.

**Save this host binding** uses the original profile revision comparison and the displayed configuration fingerprint. The browser also supplies the exact composition fingerprint. A stale revision or changed displayed composition returns `CONSOLE_REVISION_CONFLICT` or `CONSOLE_HOST_CHANGED` before any binding is added. Saving a binding preserves every original draft, call, returned value and customer record. Renaming a profile or changing a favorite retains its selected binding revision.

Each immutable binding carries its profile revision, original workspace ID, retention time, origin, full host snapshot and canonical SHA-256. **Retained host bindings** opens any earlier revision against the current host. **Export comparison** downloads the full comparison with its content digest. **Export profile** includes the complete binding history with the existing native work.

An older profile remains usable as saved. Its first explicit rebind retains the original host under `LEGACY_PROFILE`, then adds the current complete snapshot. The comparison labels a legacy baseline when exact old tool or declaration snapshots were unavailable. It still compares the old configuration, tool count, configured provider membership, dependencies and source aliases. Runtime load timing, current calls and shutdown observations are displayed on Host and excluded from the configuration comparison.

## Save, run and recover requests

Create a named profile, select a configured tool and review its actual input schema. The JSON editor contains native arguments. Existing `requestId`, workspace alias, release ID, expected digest, selection generation and file-read IDs retain their original meanings.

**Save revision** writes an immutable draft revision. Editing a saved draft requires its current revision; a concurrent change returns `CONSOLE_REVISION_CONFLICT`. **Save as new draft** creates another independently named request. A saved call always refers to its exact draft revision, including older revisions.

**Run saved revision** reserves a console call ID before entering the original operator. The reservation includes the tool-definition digest, exact argument JSON, argument SHA-256, original host binding and request digest. A repeated reservation with the same ID and exact input returns the original record. Reusing that ID with different input returns `CONSOLE_REQUEST_CONFLICT`.

The original tool performs its own source validation, generation checks, native idempotency and concurrency handling. The console records the returned value once as exact JSON text and retains its SHA-256. The browser's readable preview is separate from the **Download returned JSON** bytes.

Accepted requests appear immediately in Requests. A browser reconnect reads the existing record. If the host ended before it retained a native return, the record shows **RETURN_PENDING**. The recovery picker selects original read operations from the same configured family whose required identifiers are present in that call. It prepares a linked draft using those original identifiers. Review, save and run that original read to reconcile the native operation.

## Export and reopen operator work

**Export profile** produces a single `stellar-forge.merchant-operator-profile.v1` JSON archive containing:

- The named profile, favorite tools, selected host binding and complete immutable binding history when present.
- Every immutable saved draft revision.
- Original call IDs, exact arguments, exact returned JSON and their digests.
- Customer selection, receiving status and original file identities.
- Immutable workflow editions, complete run inputs, native step references, progress and owner-release events.

The archive has a canonical content SHA-256 and is captured in one SQLite transaction across the complete profile. When that history extends, the local profile revision advances beyond the received revisions while its selected host, name and favorites remain unchanged. Conflicting immutable source, finalized returns or divergent workflow history are rejected. [Named workflow handover](WORKFLOWS.md#hand-over-a-paused-run-and-return-it) uses this receiving path to review, transfer and return unfinished work.

Keep the private console directory to reopen the same operator database and partial customer downloads. The database uses SQLite WAL and full synchronization. It retains local identity independently of a process or listener. Imported histories retain their original workspace identity and stay distinguishable from calls accepted by the current workspace.

## Host integration contract

`createMerchantConsole({ operator, configPath, directory, authorization, bearerToken })` returns:

| Member | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `handler(req, res)` | Handles `/operator/` and its authenticated API; returns false for unrelated paths. |
| `snapshot()` | Pure configured-host snapshot with the current console identity. |
| `startCall(input, context)` | Reserves an exact native request and retains its original asynchronous return. |
| `store` | Original private profile/request SQLite store. |
| `workflows` | Saved workflow definitions, original run driver, recovery and receiving controls over that store. |
| `beginClose()` | Stops new calls, requests workflow pauses and pauses original customer transfers at retained checkpoints. |
| `close()` | Waits for accepted native returns and closes its own store after the original owner begins cancellation/drain. |

`startMerchantMcp()` owns the shared listener. On close, it refuses new interface requests, requests workflow pauses, pauses customer transfers at their original checkpoints and starts the existing merchant owner's cancellation/drain immediately. It waits for workflow drivers, accepted native returns and customer cleanup before closing the interface database and original authorization. The console never replaces the provider lifecycle or closes a separate seller owner.

The API uses the native host request capacity for saved and executed requests. The exact MCP call envelope is checked again before native dispatch, including calls imported from a profile archive. The separate history-import route accepts a complete archive up to 128 MiB; importing a history does not run its saved tools.

The following authenticated host-review routes use the same handler and authorization:

| Route | Original result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /operator/api/host-review/PROFILE` | Compare the saved profile host with the current configured snapshot. |
| `GET /operator/api/host-review/PROFILE?revision=N` | Compare one immutable retained binding revision. |
| The same route with `download=1` | Download the complete comparison and its digest. |
| `GET /operator/api/host-binding/PROFILE?revision=N` | Read the exact immutable binding record. |
| `POST /operator/api/bind` | Original revision-guarded bind with optional `expectedCompositionFingerprint`. |

The existing profile read includes compact binding-history summaries. Its existing `hostBound` describes the configuration binding; `compositionBound` separately describes the saved declaration/tool snapshot and is `null` for a legacy snapshot. A changed declaration is available for review, and original native tool admission remains the authority for execution. `compareHostProfiles(before, after)` and `captureHostComposition(...)` in `host-profile.mjs` are pure metadata functions. `MerchantConsoleStore.hostBindings()` and `.hostBinding()` read the original SQLite history.

Static assets use the original loopback host, same-origin requests and a restrictive content-security policy. There are no external scripts, fonts or image dependencies.

### Continue the same customer through a host review

The following receiver consumes the completed original directory above. It opens that same operator database, migrates its actual legacy profile on explicit rebind, compares a real configuration copy with an additional alias for the original SF61 source, retains both complete bindings and reopens the exact saved customer. It then exports and receives the profile with its full original draft/call/customer and binding history.

```sh

  --console-receiving /private/receiving/merchant-console \

  --chromium /absolute/path/to/chromium \
  --playwright-module /absolute/path/to/playwright \
  --source-commit REVIEWED_SOURCE_COMMIT
```

The driver retains each binding intent before the original mutation and reconciles its revision and exact target after an uncertain response. Restarting the same receiving directory resumes the recorded phase. The original configuration file and its source bytes remain the input; the changed profile uses a separate configuration file in that same private merchant directory so all original relative paths resolve identically.

Outputs include `host-review-native-run.json`, a durable phase checkpoint, the original and changed comparison exports, the complete profile with binding history, the unchanged customer archive and desktop/mobile browser views. The driver uses the original authenticated HTTP/UI and SQLite implementation. Reading archived results and comparing metadata does not create another seller, native search or customer-export operation.


The complete saved-workflow receiver is `receiving/workflow-journey.mjs`. Its [native receiving instructions](WORKFLOWS.md#run-the-complete-native-receiving-workflow) cover the original seven-step merchant operation, browser action recovery, named workspace transfer and return, complete profile receiving and customer files. Use its selected source and existing native runtime for that original operation.

The same following receiver also returns the complete newer archive to a console that already received the original profile. It checks exact historical binding bodies, retained local host/name/favorites, the advanced receiving revision, duplicate reuse and another cold reopen. `host-review-returned-profile.json` and its browser view retain that complete round trip.


## Original reviewer customer delivery

The configured grant reviewer family now has a complete Customers operating page: original packet intake, retained Buyer history and complete result/source files, explicit closed export, independent receiving, and fourteen-step delivery/six-step receiving recipes in the existing Workflow engine. See [Reviewer Customer Delivery](CUSTOMER_REVIEWER.md) for the original lifecycle, full-file handoff and restartable Console receiving command. # TokenJunkieLabs Stellar merchant workspace

Build and operate a data service with Stellar payment access, native customer
clients, retained source results, deployment releases, and an operator workspace.

The product brings together captured HTTP API and GraphQL service authoring,
Kafka event datasets, reviewed aid-finance portfolios, satellite imagery and
processing history, searchable
material catalogs, merchant incident work, supplier cost allocation and pricing
decisions, and QuickBooks or Xero accounting operations. Each workflow keeps its
original saved records from source selection through delivery and reopening.

The [development architecture and delivery plan](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/main/products/merchant-workspace/DEVELOPMENT.md)
connects the original code, user interfaces, prospective Stellar integration
roadmap, native acceptance and complete customer handover in one source.

## Choose a workflow

| Work to complete | Entry point | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complete recurring customer periods and source changes | **Merchant operator → Workflows → Recurring customer work** or `starforge merchant-workflow-series` | [Saved customer series](../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/console/WORKFLOW_SERIES.md), exact original cycle runs, full prior-period history, operator handover and complete customer-file receiving |
| Receive Baserow data into a Rails application | **Applications → Baserow source authoring** and `starforge baserow-rails` | [Complete selected installation](../baserow-rails/README.md), original source editions and attachments, typed Ruby receiving, transactional Rails preview/import and full application handover |
| Set up and operate a WooCommerce / CoCart customer | `starforge cocart-setup` and **Applications → CoCart** | Original saved-profile or whole-customer intake, native cart and Woo checkout, managed reopening and complete receiving |
| Turn captured HTTP API traffic into a merchant | `starforge captured-api` | Original source review, exact route prices, native merchant packages, release operations and complete receiving |
| Operate purchased API access | `starforge api-pass-workspace` and `starforge merchant-api-pass` | One saved customer, original purchases and requests, browser/agent operation and complete response receiving |
| Operate and hand over buyer request collections | **Applications → Request collections** or `starforge buyer-collections-workspace` | Reviewed original requests, exact spending caps and outcomes, complete encrypted backup, receiving and reopening |
| Operate a saved merchant fleet | **Applications → Merchant fleet** or `starforge merchant-fleet-workspace` | Reviewed source releases, controlled activation and drain, client delivery, durable settlement delivery, and encrypted recovery with the original fleet state |
| Turn an existing GraphQL query service into a merchant | **Applications → GraphQL merchant workspace** or `starforge graphql-product` | Reviewed source operations, buyer clients, deployment releases and complete project history that reopens for continued authoring |
| Receive a complete OData query into customer analysis | **Applications → OData source and live merchant** or `starforge dataset odata --workspace DIRECTORY serve` | Retained source/query, complete ordered live-page collection, original Analysis/report/workbook and full workspace receiving |
| Turn Kafka events into a dataset and merchant | `starforge dataset-kafka`, `starforge kafka-client` and the Kafka merchant tools | Exact retained topic history, mapped editions, native query/merchant packages and resumable complete customer receiving |
| Operate a Timescale data product | **Applications → Timescale merchant workspace** or `starforge timescale-agent` | Native editions, refresh and job review, exact publication, assigned work, complete reports and portable customer receiving |
| Operate a Huwise data product | `starforge huwise`, `starforge merchant-huwise` and `starforge merchant-huwise-receive` | Complete portal editions, analyst review, tenant ingestion and publication, native merchant operation and full customer receiving |
| Prepare imagery and processing data for customers | `starforge stac` | Retained scene editions and assets, Cirrus or FilmDrop history, original merchant/customer delivery and a portable GIS explorer |
| Operate a searchable material catalog | `starforge-materials` | The maintained catalog, source review, operator workspace, query service and customer receiving |
| Allocate supplier costs and operate merchant pricing | **Applications → Merchant pricing and scenario planning** or `starforge revenue-workspace` | Original bills and quotes, exact route allocations, cost-linked pricing and scenarios, reviewed seller changes and complete workspace receiving |
| [Operate complete Merchant Support](../merchant-support/README.md) | **Applications → Merchant support**, `starforge support-console`, or the original merchant agent | Saved cases and incidents, implementation and source editions, service commitments, quotations, complete customer packages and independently continued receiving |
| Work with a selected accounting destination | `starforge merchant-accounting-platforms` | Original QuickBooks or Xero plans, reviewed requests, provider responses and accountant returns |
| Open an issued buyer period for accounting | `starforge merchant-accounting-workspace buyer init` and the accounting browser | Complete retained buyer source, the same saved handoff, explicit accounting decisions, original returns and encrypted recovery |
| Review a changed QuickBooks or Xero chart | **Accounting → Chart source changes** or `starforge accounting-source-changes` | Both original company-chart editions, reviewed mappings and valuations, and a recoverable replacement of the selected unused plan |
| Review aid-finance publisher data and hand it over | **Applications → IATI aid finance** or `starforge dataset-iati` | Complete original XML editions, exact financial groups, named portfolio review, browser/MCP/CLI operation and portable customer receiving |

The [operator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/main/products/merchant-workspace/OPERATING.md)

## Open the source product

Use Linux, Node.js 22.16 or later, Git, and util-linux `flock`.
Retained workspaces need a local filesystem that supports file locks, atomic
rename, and fsync.

~~~sh
git clone https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace.git
cd tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/cli.mjs --help
~~~

The source paths are preserved. Before installation, replace `starforge` in
the commands below with:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/cli.mjs
~~~

For example, start a private imagery workspace against an actual public catalog:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/cli.mjs stac init \
  --workspace /absolute/private/imagery \
  --title 'Imagery operations' \
  --endpoint https://earth-search.aws.element84.com/v1

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/cli.mjs stac serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/imagery --port 0
~~~

Open the local URL printed by the server. Discover the catalog, save an area and
time selection, review the source request, and acquire its scene pages. The
workspace retains the original provider responses, scene identities, geometry,
and selected image files. Reopening saved work uses those retained files.

## Create and install a source archive

The maintained builder packages one selected Git revision and its complete
declared source. Run it from the product checkout:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo . --ref HEAD --out /absolute/private/packages/merchant
~~~

Keep the returned archive, its SHA-256, and its manifest together. The package
contains the original source, browser assets, command registrations, API exports,
selected README, and licenses.

For a source-only installation in a new application directory:

~~~sh
npm install --ignore-scripts --offline --omit=optional /absolute/path/to/package.tgz
npx --no-install starforge doctor
~~~

Source-only installation supports the features that use Node's built-in modules.
The runtime installer adds the declared dependencies for selected database,
GraphQL, MCP, payment, and other adapters. Choose the feature set for the actual
merchant; the installed package supplies the exact dependency declarations.

A GraphQL merchant operated through MCP normally selects the GraphQL, schema,
OpenAPI, and MCP features, plus the native Stellar packages:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-install prepare \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/query-merchant \
  --archive /srv/starforge/downloads/merchant.tgz \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature graphql --feature schema --feature openapi --feature mcp \
  --operator

starforge runtime-install install \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/query-merchant

starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /srv/starforge/runtimes/query-merchant -- source
~~~

Use the actual archive path and hash returned by the builder. The original
installer retains its lock, dependency selection, installation progress and
recovery state. Its
[installation guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/main/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/RUNTIME_INSTALL.md)
covers interruption, native prerequisites, upgrades, and reopening. The

provides the corresponding browser workflow.

## Operate one saved merchant

For a captured HTTP API, initialize and open its private product:

~~~sh
starforge captured-api init --dir /absolute/private/captured-api \
  --name 'Supplier API'
starforge captured-api open --dir /absolute/private/captured-api --browser-only
~~~

Upload the original HAR, review operations in the browser, and save the immutable
source decisions. Use that approved source in the native merchant form, set the
payment and upstream choices, and review exact route prices in its worksheet.
Compile and save the complete merchant, then reopen its original package for
release and customer receiving. Opening the same product with its MCP token
enables the HAR and OpenAPI agent workflows against that same browser and state.
The captured API guide gives the full runtime selection and commands.

For an existing query service:

1. Open the GraphQL workspace and capture the actual served schema.
2. Select query fields and buyer-variable bounds, then preview the approved
   operation against its configured source.
3. Save the merchant plan with the intended public routes and payment choices.
4. Review and export the saved project. The export includes the original query,
   source binding, seller files, generated buyer client, and request examples.
5. Prepare the deployment, stage its release, select it, and start the original
   merchant. Keep the release and host records with the workspace.
6. Reopen the same project when the source schema or service changes. Compare
   against its retained export before preparing a revised release.

The browser and merchant MCP tools operate the same saved project, revisions,
preview UUIDs, exports, and deployment records. A completed source preview can be
opened again without making another provider request. The
[GraphQL product guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/main/products/graphql-workspace/OPERATING.md)
and
[MCP operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/main/stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/GRAPHQL_WORKSPACES.md)
give the exact configuration and action contracts.

## Keep the operating state

Keep workspace directories, configuration files, original request records, and
completed delivery files outside the source checkout. Supply credential values
through the host's environment or existing secret manager; configuration files
retain their reference names.

Use the product's original export and receiving commands for a handover. Imagery
deliveries include a local scene explorer and retained selected assets. Captured API
handoffs keep the native capture or refresh directory, immutable reviews, full
merchant package and pricing worksheet. GraphQL project handovers retain every
committed revision through the selected revision, completed source previews,
generated clients and original deployment files. The receiving operator reopens
the same project and prepares a deployment for the receiving installation. Pricing and supplier-cost handoffs use the
original complete workspace backup to retain supplier originals, cost editions,
pricing reviews, scenario comparisons and price decisions together. Support
handoffs carry the original captures and saved case. Accounting operations keep
their original request and response identities through reconciliation.

Use a fresh runtime directory for an upgrade, select its original source
archive, then attach the existing operating state through that workflow's
supported configuration. Retain the previous runtime and selected release until
the replacement is operating as intended.

    'After COMPLETE upload, start IMPORT, retain its job and manifest, create a RECEIVING draft and save its complete names with merchant_handover_receiving_save. '+
    'For an incoming edition, start COMPARE from the saved receiving draft with installed baseline overrides; page merchant_handover_editions for full plan, exact prices, source/facade, configuration and file changes. '+

    'REOPEN the saved receiving operation after restart and use merchant_har_load for the original saved merchant/source. '+
    'Whole files travel through the original stream/upload engines; small archive_read chunks are for explicit file consumers. '+
    'The companion drains its own accepted calls. The existing product retains browser, seller, agent and source ownership.'}],
  load:()=>import('./handover-agent.mjs'),
  create:(module,config,options)=>new module.MerchantCapturedHandovers(config,{environment:options.environment}),

// MIT. Metadata for the original release-store destination and receiving tools.
import { MAX_RETAINED_CHUNK_BYTES } from '../retained-file-contracts.mjs';
const digest = { type: 'string', pattern: '^[a-f0-9]{64}$' };
const transfer = { type: 'string', pattern: '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$' };
const destination = { type: 'string', pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$' };
const identity = { type: 'string', minLength: 1, maxLength: 128 };
export function deliveryTools(tool) {
  const settings = { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, properties: {
    id: destination, label: { type: 'string', minLength: 1, maxLength: 100 },
    url: { type: 'string', minLength: 1, maxLength: 4096 },
    allowedHost: { type: 'string', minLength: 1, maxLength: 253 },
    secretEnv: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,64}$' },
    routeIds: { type: 'array', maxItems: 100, uniqueItems: true,
      items: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80}$' } },
    networks: { type: 'array', maxItems: 32, uniqueItems: true,
      items: { type: 'string', pattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}:[A-Za-z0-9:_-]{1,100}$' } },
    history: { type: 'string', enum: ['all', 'new'] }, paused: { type: 'boolean' },
    expectedRevision: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1 }, eventId: digest, expectedDeliveryRevision: digest,
    limit: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 100 },
    concurrency: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 16 },
    destinationConcurrency: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 16 },
    timeoutMs: { type: 'integer', minimum: 100, maximum: 60000 },
    pollMs: { type: 'integer', minimum: 100, maximum: 60000 },
  } };
  return [
    tool('merchant_delivery_status', 'Read the configured single release store’s original settlement producer, journal warnings, destination cursors, worker and lease. Start that original seller once to initialize its retained source.',
      {}, [], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_delivery_control', 'Operate that store’s original SF98 destination workspace. Enroll uses a signing environment reference and explicit all/new history; pause/requeue use inspected revisions. Sync copies original receipts. Drain/start send through the original signed HTTPS transport.',
      { action: { type: 'string', enum: ['enroll', 'pause', 'sync', 'drain', 'start', 'stop', 'requeue'] }, input: settings },
      ['action', 'input'], { openWorld: true }),
    tool('merchant_delivery_stop', 'Stop the original destination worker through its existing stop operation. This control remains callable while another host operation is awaiting delivery.',
      {}, [], { idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_delivery_events', 'Page one original destination’s event IDs, settlement payloads, outcomes and maintenance revisions.',
      { id: destination, state: { type: 'string', enum: ['ALL', 'PENDING', 'DELIVERED', 'RETRY', 'REQUEUE', 'EXHAUSTED'] },
        offset: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0 }, limit: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 200 } },
      ['id'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_delivery_handoff', 'Read the original delivery workspace handoff, source continuity, destination cursors and environment references.',
      {}, [], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_delivery_transfers', 'List retained immutable SF98 exchanges. They remain available independently of the live source and include original receiving arguments.',
      { after: transfer, limit: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: 50 } },
      [], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_delivery_transfer', 'Capture the source fingerprint last reviewed in delivery status under a chosen transfer ID. After a lost response, repeat the same ID and fingerprint to reopen its exact retained capture.',
      { id: transfer, expectedSourceFingerprint: digest }, ['id', 'expectedSourceFingerprint'], { idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_delivery_manifest', 'Inspect the original retained exchange and each native file’s exact bytes and SHA-256. Use the exchange fingerprint for download and original receiving.',
      { id: transfer, expectedFingerprint: digest }, ['id'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_delivery_file', 'Read an original retained exchange member through the existing verified reader. Repeat its inspected fingerprint, relative name and SHA-256; use readId and offset to continue.',
      { id: transfer, expectedFingerprint: digest, expectedSha256: digest,
        name: { type: 'string', pattern: '^(?:manifest\\.json|source/(?:manifest\\.json|events\\.ndjson|deliveries\\.ndjson)|destinations/[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,47}/(?:manifest\\.json|events\\.ndjson|deliveries\\.ndjson))$' },
        readId: identity, offset: { type: 'integer', minimum: 0 },
        limit: { type: 'integer', minimum: 1, maximum: MAX_RETAINED_CHUNK_BYTES } },
      ['id', 'expectedFingerprint', 'name', 'expectedSha256'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
    tool('merchant_delivery_file_release', 'Close this store and transfer’s temporary file read while preserving the original exchange for receiving or resumed download.',
      { id: transfer, readId: identity }, ['id', 'readId'], { readOnly: true, idempotent: true }),
  ];
}
